title: Network nodes allowed in right-of-way without zoning review
summary: A network provider may construct, modify and collocate network nodes and node support poles in a municipal right-of-way as a permitted use, subject to permit and codes.
locator: Enrolled S.B. 1004, new Local Gov’t Code § 284.101(a)
evidence: without need for a special use permit or similar zoning review
issuer: Texas Legislature (S.B. 1004, 85th Leg., Local Government Code ch. 284)
brief: 2017 enacted text; current law unverified. Network providers may build network nodes in a city right-of-way as a permitted use, without special use permit or zoning review.
scope_basis: General rule for the providers and work specified in this record; it is not written specifically for data centers.
status_reported: Enrolled bill text, 85th Legislature (2017); later amendments not checked
source_title: Enrolled S.B. 1004, 85th Texas Legislature (network nodes in public right-of-way)
hold_reason: Only the 2017 enrolled act is archived; current amendments are unverified.

title: Cities may require a general permit for nodes and transport facilities
summary: A municipality may require a permit for a network node, node support pole or transport facility only if it applies generally to right-of-way users and is processed without discrimination.

brief: 2017 enacted text; current law unverified. A city may require a right-of-way permit for network nodes and transport facilities if it applies to all right-of-way users.

title: Completeness check within 30 days for network node permits

locator: Enrolled S.B. 1004, new Local Gov’t Code § 284.154(b)

issuer: Texas Legislature (S.B. 1004, 85th Leg., Local Government Code ch. 284)

title: Annual right-of-way rate capped at $250 per network node
summary: The annual public right-of-way rate for network nodes may not exceed $250 multiplied by the number of network nodes installed in the municipality.
locator: Enrolled S.B. 1004, new Local Gov’t Code § 284.053(a)
evidence: may not exceed an annual amount equal to $250 multiplied by the number of network nodes
issuer: Texas Legislature (S.B. 1004, 85th Leg., Local Government Code ch. 284)
brief: 2017 enacted text; current law unverified. A city may charge no more than $250 per network node per year for right-of-way use.
